description: Look up registered media (MIME) types. Pass exactly one of `type` (a full name such as "application/json"; parameters after ";" are ignored) or `keyword` (words matched against registered type names and status annotations, e.g. "geo json"; never against file extensions). An exact `type` lookup also reads the registration template and returns its file-extension, intended-usage, and deprecated-alias statements as written, each only when the template has it. Some registered types have no registration template (`template.available: false`); their references are the defining documents. Deprecated and obsoleted types are reported with their replacement when the registry names one. Unregistered "x-" types are not in the registry.

keyword.description: Words matched as whole tokens against registered type names and status annotations, e.g. "geo json". File extensions are not searched: look up the expected type with type to read its template's file-extension statement, when the template has one. Pass this or type, not both.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return, 1–100. Default 25.

offset.description: Number of keyword matches to skip; pass the next_offset of the previous response to get the next page. Default 0.

top_level.description: Keep only types under this top-level type, e.g. "image". Keyword mode only.

type.description: Full media type, case-insensitive, e.g. "application/json" ("; charset=utf-8" and other parameters are dropped). Pass this or keyword, not both.

name: iana_lookup_media_type

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `mode_required`: Neither or both of type and keyword were given. `upstream_unreadable`: The media type registry file could not be fetched or parsed. `pacer_shed`: This server's own iana.org request queue is too full for the call to start in time. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

found.description: True when a registered media type matched.

media_types.description: Matching media types: exact name hits first, then registry order.

id.description: E.g. "RFC 9110", a draft name, a registry id, or a URL.

label.description: Label text, when it adds to id and section.

replaced_by.description: The replacement type the annotation names.

status.description: From the registry annotation (OBSOLETE(D), DEPRECATED); else current.

status_note.description: The status annotation, e.g. "OBSOLETED in favor of text/javascript".

template.description: Type mode: the registration template read; each statement absent when the template lacks it.

available.description: True when a template was read; false when IANA publishes no registration template for this type, so its references are its defining documents. Absent when fetched is false.

deprecated_aliases.description: The "Deprecated alias names for this type" statement.

fetched.description: False when the template could not be read.

file_extensions.description: The "File extension(s)" statement as written, e.g. ".json".

next_offset.description: Pass as offset for the next page; absent on the last.

normalized_type.description: Type mode: the type looked up, lowercased, parameters removed.

notice.description: Guidance on a miss, a cut list, or another condition.

source.description: Provenance and freshness of the answer.

fetched_at.description: ISO 8601 time of the last successful fetch or revalidation.

registry_id.description: Id of the registry file that answered.

registry_updated.description: The registry's own last-updated date; absent for the protocol index.

stale.description: True when a refresh failed and a cached copy up to 7 days old answered.

totalCount.description: Matches before the limit was applied.

truncated.description: True when more matches exist than were returned.

title: Look up a media type
